about:
Canonical twin layout for the assembled page -> layout/twin-layout.json.

Coordinate frame: the X3D world frame of scenes/cabinet.x3d itself. Metres, +Y up, right-handed, +Z points toward
the Overview camera (position 0 3.3 8.4), origin at the centre of the floor slab top. The seven bays sit on an arc of
radius 6.5 m about the floor point (0, 0, 3), azimuth -60 deg (Bay1, left) to +60 deg (Bay7, right), azimuth measured
in the XZ plane from -Z toward +X about that point. Anything drawn in these coordinates can be added to the X3D scene
(or a WebGL overlay with the same camera) without conversion.

Three strata (DESIGN section 1):
  objects   world position of every scene individual (DEF, USE copy, positional/unnamed node), from composing the
            Transform chain in Python (translation, center, rotation, scaleOrientation, scale; X3D 4.1 order).
            Shape, Appearance, Material, texture and geometry nodes take their Shape's frame origin (the centre of the
            primitive); Viewpoint and PointLight take their position/location field; Scene-level nodes without a
            position (WorldInfo, NavigationInfo, Background, DirectionalLight) and the document nodes (X3D, head,
            meta, component, Scene) are placed on a labelled shelf in front of the arc centre (spatial = false).
  twin      one bead per individual: x,z = its object's x,z, y = 2.4 m + 0.17 m per tree level below the Scene's
            children, then a deterministic relaxation (fixed order, fixed iterations) pushes beads of the same level
            apart to >= 0.16 m in XZ while a spring keeps them near their object.
  ontology  every class in ontology/classes.json on a dome over the arc. The ring is the class's HEIGHT in the
            shown hierarchy (longest rdfs:subClassOf chain down to a shown subclass; classes with no shown subclass,
            i.e. the concrete node types, are height 0): height 0 is the lowest ring (y = 4.3 m, radius 7.2 m, just
            behind and above the bays, so rdf:type plumb lines are short), each ring up adds 0.6 m and takes 0.95 m
            off the radius, the roots sit highest. Azimuth = the circular mean of the class's instances (or of its
            subclasses), then each ring is de-collided to a minimum chord of 0.85 m inside azimuth [-110, 110] deg;
            a ring with more than 12 classes alternates two rows (every second class 0.3 m higher, 0.4 m further in).
Edges are the explicit triples to draw (field threads, sameAs threads, rdf:type plumb lines, subClassOf along the
dome, ROUTE arcs). hasParent edges are listed with draw=false: each is the inverse of a has<Field> edge.
Variants: only what differs from the Cabinet (new individuals placed against the fixed Cabinet layout, removed IRIs,
edge differences), so shared IRIs keep one position on every scene.

frame.origin: floor centre (the floor slab top is y = 0)
frame.azimuth: degrees in XZ from -Z toward +X about arc_centre_xz

overview_camera.note: the scene Viewpoint Overview: frames floor and twin; the dome is above its frame

twin_camera.note: suggested page camera (not in the X3D scene): floor, twin and dome in one frame

fault-F2.what: Shape geometry removed (Bare Specimen loses its Box)

fault-F3.what: Wrong-type USE: the Lantern base's PhysicalMaterial USE points at the PixelTexture DEF 'Weave'

fault-F5.what: Box directly under a Transform (containerField='children'), appended to PrismShelf

fault-F6.what: USE before DEF: OrbB (USE Gilt) moved before OrbA (DEF Gilt)

fault-F7.what: Duplicate DEF: the Jade prism's Material renamed DEF 'Ruby'

teach-exponent.what: Teaching variant: the F1 colour 1.5 written as 0.15e1 (exponent form)

teach-insert.what: Teaching variant (not a fault): one unnamed DirectionalLight inserted first in the Scene
